Quick triage from CS side: Impacted flows are predominantly checkout prompt routes for StellarPay. Traffic volume itself is normal; errors correlate with long-lived user sessions (many calls with long context length).

From logs: we see elevated allocation/residency on several GPU workers, and a handful of OOM events followed by node restarts. The pattern looks like progressive GPU memory fragmentation/KV cache growth rather than a single spike in per-request memory.

Immediate mitigations suggested:
- Short-term: route StellarPay's traffic to the quantized model variant (longform-v1-q4) to reduce per-token memory.
- Force periodic KV cache eviction for sessions older than 30m for this customer.
- If allowed, schedule rolling restarts on 10% of the pool to clear fragmentation.

I attached the debug-log-0406.txt with the OOM traces and a pointer to the grafana spike.

Marissa

Technical notes from runtime: confirmed multiple OOMs on GPU hosts serving longform-v1. Symptoms:
- Memory fragmentation increasing over time on hosts with long-running sessions; fragmentation reduces effective free memory despite low RSS in some cases.
- KV cache for multi-turn chats exceeds expected bounds for certain session heuristics when prompts hit >12k tokens.
- Auto-scaler observed higher latency and throttled throughput as retries increased, causing queuing.

Actions taken (immediate):
1) Routed StellarPay tenant traffic to longform-v1-q4 (quantized) at 17:12 PT (fall back to high-quality later).
2) Enabled a per-tenant KV eviction policy (evict sessions >30m idle) for StellarPay at 17:20 PT.
3) Performed a rolling restart of 8% of the affected serving fleet (safe-window restarts) starting 17:35 PT; node restarts cleared fragmented allocations.

Suggested follow-ups (owner):
- infra/runtime: patch the allocator and add periodic compaction routine (JIRA INF-1234) — owner: jonas_weber.
- product: evaluate whether longform-v1 should expose documented per-session limits or a memory-protecting mode — owner: laura_bennett.
- cs: offer StellarPay an operational credit and a postmortem call — owner: marissa_cole.

We will monitor for 24 hours. Early telemetry shows p99 trending back toward baseline (~1s) after the routing and restarts; will update.

-Rishi
Lead Runtime Engineer
